title: Heinberg's Young Avengers
proposed_why: A young Kang the Conqueror travels back in time to escape his destiny and assembles a new team from the Avengers' legacy — Patriot, Hulkling, Wiccan, Stature, Kate Bishop as Hawkeye and later Speed — and Allan Heinberg and Jim Cheung make them one of the best teen teams in comics. The mysteries of who Hulkling and Wiccan really are lead straight to the Kree, the Skrulls and the Scarlet Witch. Dark Reign: Young Avengers, by Paul Cornell, pits them against a team of imposters.

title: Children's Crusade
proposed_why: Wiccan's powers are growing like his mother's, and when the Avengers talk about stopping him the way they stopped the Scarlet Witch, he and Speed go looking for Wanda herself — with Magneto along, and Doctor Doom waiting at the end of the trail. title: Gillen's Loki
proposed_why: Kieron Gillen's Journey into Mystery on its own: Loki reborn as a child who remembers nothing of his crimes, trying to prove he can be good while Asgard waits for him to turn, and a magpie with his old self's voice whispering in his ear. It's clever, funny and heartbreaking, and it builds through Fear Itself and Exiled to Everything Burns and one of the most devastating endings Marvel published that decade. The run that made Loki a hero readers cared about.

title: Gillen's Young Avengers

proposed_why: Kieron Gillen and Jamie McKelvie reunite Wiccan and Hulkling with Kid Loki, Miss America, Kate Bishop and Marvel Boy, and send them after an interdimensional parasite Wiccan unleashed trying to bring back Hulkling's mother. It's a book about being young, in love and a bit of a mess, told with pop-art layouts and the energy of a great indie record. The most stylish superhero book of its decade — and Vengeance, which opens the order, is where America Chavez debuts.
